name: Disable Remote Desktop
description: Refuses all incoming Remote Desktop connections. If you never use RDP this closes a service that is a standing target for credential-stuffing attacks.

name: Enable Remote Desktop
description: Allows incoming Remote Desktop connections. Pair this with Network Level Authentication and a strong password, and do not expose port 3389 to the internet directly.

name: Require Network Level Authentication for RDP
description: Makes clients authenticate before a session and a full desktop are set up. Without NLA an unauthenticated attacker can reach far more of the RDP stack.

name: Require High Encryption for RDP
description: Sets the RDP minimum encryption level to High, so sessions must use 128-bit encryption in both directions.

name: Disable RDP Clipboard Sharing
description: Stops the clipboard being shared between the remote session and the client machine, which is a common accidental data-exfiltration path.

name: Disable RDP Drive Redirection
description: Stops a connecting client mapping its local drives into the remote session.

name: Disable RDP Printer Redirection
description: Stops client printers being mapped into remote sessions, which also stops the print driver being installed on the host.

name: Disconnect Idle RDP Sessions After 15 Minutes
description: Ends idle remote sessions rather than leaving an authenticated desktop sitting open indefinitely.

name: Limit RDP to One Session Per User
description: Stops one account holding several simultaneous remote sessions, so a reconnect resumes the existing desktop instead of opening another.

name: Disable Remote Assistance
description: Turns off the legacy Remote Assistance invitation mechanism, which is separate from Remote Desktop and rarely used deliberately.

name: Disable Basic Authentication for WinRM
description: Stops Windows Remote Management accepting Basic auth, which sends the password with only base64 encoding around it.

name: Require Encrypted WinRM Traffic
description: Refuses unencrypted WinRM sessions in both the client and service roles.

name: Disable the WinRM Service
description: Stops the Windows Remote Management listener starting. Do not apply this on a machine you administer remotely with PowerShell Remoting.

name: Disable the Remote Registry Service
description: Stops other machines reading or writing this PC's registry over the network. Off by default on client Windows; this makes sure it stays off.

name: Disable Administrative Shares (C$, ADMIN$)
description: Removes the hidden C$ and ADMIN$ shares Windows creates automatically. Closes a well-worn lateral-movement path; also breaks remote management tools that rely on them.

name: Block Anonymous Access to Shares and Pipes
description: Stops unauthenticated 'null sessions' enumerating shares and named pipes, a classic reconnaissance step on a Windows network.

name: Block Remote Admin Rights for Local Accounts
description: Keeps LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy off, so a local administrator account connecting over the network gets a filtered token rather than full admin rights. This is the setting that makes pass-the-hash against local accounts much harder.

name: Disable Wi-Fi Direct Services
description: Disables the Wi-Fi Direct Services Connection Manager, which handles peer-to-peer connections to wireless displays and printers. Turn it off if you never cast to a Miracast display.

name: Disable Peer-to-Peer Networking Services
description: Disables the Peer Networking Identity Manager and Grouping services used by Windows Meeting Space and HomeGroup-era features that nothing modern needs.

name: Block Quick Assist
description: Prevents the Quick Assist remote help tool being used on this machine. Quick Assist is a favourite of tech-support scammers precisely because it is built in and needs no install.

name: Disable the RDP UDP Transport
description: Forces Remote Desktop onto TCP only. Fixes flickering and disconnects on links where the UDP path is unreliable, at some cost in responsiveness on a good connection.

name: Do Not Save Remote Desktop Credentials
description: Stops the Remote Desktop client offering to remember passwords, so they are not stored in Credential Manager for anyone with your session to reuse.
